labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 1, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. The plate map checks what each well holds, not what plate it is.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 5 biology problems (1 error, 2 warnings, 2 notes).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 80:  p20.aspirate(10.5, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 80 the p20_single_gen2 draws 10.5 ul from water (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip
   1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 184 ul, which in this NEST 12
   Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.87 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air
   (this line did it 13 times, after 11 times in the liquid; 136 ul of air in all). The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 13 wells filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 13 other wells: wells B6, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, D1 and 5 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [5eeda556d001]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A1 in slot 4)
   line 80:  p20.aspirate(10.5, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 80 the tip went into water (well A1 in slot 4) while it still carried master mix
   (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a
   little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does
   not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that
   were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 80 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [62b0a0c7396b]

3. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 24 stocks
   line 83:  p20.aspirate(2, sample_source)
   At line 83 the tip went into sample 1 (tube A1 in slot 2), sample 2 (tube A2 in slot 2),
   sample 3 (tube A3 in slot 2), sample 4 (tube A4 in slot 2) and 20 more while it still
   carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3) and water (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step
   (this line did it 24 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in
   the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there.
   The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left
   in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: tubes A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 83 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [265791f35d7f]

4. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 24 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 78:  p20.dispense(12.5, target_well)
   At line 78 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   1), and 24 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in
   slot 1.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [57a68efc8d68]

5. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 24 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4
and 20 more went in (8 to 14% of the well)
   line 84:  p20.dispense(2, target_well)
   At line 84 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 20 more to wells
   A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1, which already held master mix and
   water (this line did it 24 times). The addition was 8 to 14% of the well, nothing mixed
   the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one
   will not be, mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2 and 16 more in slot 1 after line 84:
   `mix_after=(5, 12 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 12 to 20, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [b3a5be2528f1]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: water (well A1 in slot 4)
findings.explanation: At line 80 the tip went into water (well A1 in slot 4) while it still carried master mix (tube A1 in slot 3) from an earlier step. A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 80 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
